interactions.title: Extreme Bleeding Risk: NSAIDs + Multiple Blood Thinners
interactions.description: Ibuprofen at 1,800 mg/day inhibits platelet function. Combining with aged garlic (7,500 mg — potent blood thinner), krill oil (omega-3s thin blood), nattokinase (fibrinolytic enzyme), turmeric/curcumin (antiplatelet), and black seed oil (anticoagulant properties) creates a compounding bleeding risk. Each of these alone has mild-to-moderate anticoagulant effects; together they significantly increase risk of GI bleeds, bruising, and hemorrhage.
interactions.recommendation: This combination should be reviewed by a physician immediately. At minimum, reduce the number of blood-thinning agents taken concurrently.

interactions.title: Vitamin D3 Toxicity Risk at 100,000 IU/day
interactions.description: 100,000 IU daily of D3 is far above the upper tolerable intake of 4,000 IU/day and even above the weekly bolus doses (50,000 IU/week) used therapeutically. This can cause hypercalcemia — dangerously high calcium levels leading to kidney stones, arterial calcification, nausea, confusion, and cardiac arrhythmias. While K2 helps direct calcium away from arteries, it cannot fully compensate for this level of D3. The multivitamin adds another ~800 IU.
interactions.recommendation: Require serum 25(OH)D and calcium levels. This dose should only be used short-term under medical supervision for documented severe deficiency.

interactions.title: Extreme Iodine Dose: Thyroid Disruption Risk
interactions.description: 300 mg (300,000 mcg) of iodine is approximately 2,000 times the RDA (150 mcg) and 273 times the upper tolerable limit (1,100 mcg). This can cause thyroid storm, hypothyroidism (Wolff-Chaikoff effect), or hyperthyroidism (Jod-Basedow phenomenon). The multivitamin adds additional iodine. Kelp/seaweed in other supplements may contribute more.
interactions.recommendation: This dose is dangerous without close endocrinologist supervision and regular thyroid function testing (TSH, free T3, free T4).

interactions.title: Zinc-Copper Imbalance
interactions.description: 100 mg of zinc picolinate is 2.5x the upper tolerable limit (40 mg). The multivitamin adds another 7.5 mg. High zinc intake blocks copper absorption, leading to copper deficiency anemia and neurological problems. The 2 mg copper supplement and ~0.75 mg from the multi (total ~2.75 mg) are insufficient to balance ~107.5 mg of zinc. Ideal zinc:copper ratio is 10-15:1; this stack is ~39:1.
interactions.recommendation: Reduce zinc to 30-50 mg/day or increase copper supplementation. Monitor serum zinc, copper, and ceruloplasmin levels.

interactions.title: NSAIDs + GI-Irritating Supplements
interactions.description: Ibuprofen at 1,800 mg/day already carries significant GI risk (ulcers, gastritis). Oil of oregano (6,000 mg — extremely high) is caustic to the GI lining. Aged garlic at high doses and turmeric/ginger can also irritate the stomach. Combined, these dramatically increase the risk of GI ulceration and bleeding.
interactions.recommendation: Take ibuprofen with food and consider a PPI if chronic use is needed. Reduce oregano oil dose significantly.

interactions.title: Multiple Blood-Pressure-Lowering Agents: Hypotension Risk
interactions.description: This stack contains numerous agents that lower blood pressure: magnesium (vasodilator), potassium (counteracts sodium), olive leaf/oleuropein (ACE-inhibitor-like), beetroot (nitric oxide), aged garlic (vasodilator), moringa (blood-pressure-lowering), and black seed oil (antihypertensive). Taking all of these together may cause excessive blood pressure drops, dizziness, and fainting, especially when standing.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure regularly. If already on BP medication, this combination could cause dangerous hypotension.

interactions.title: Multiple Blood-Sugar-Lowering Agents: Hypoglycemia Risk
interactions.description: Berberine (in BurnSlim) is as potent as metformin for blood sugar reduction. Moringa, black seed oil, chromium (in the multi), and ALCAR also lower blood sugar. Stacking these creates risk of hypoglycemia, especially if fasting or on diabetes medication.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood glucose. If diabetic or pre-diabetic, coordinate with physician.

interactions.title: Boron Above Upper Tolerable Limit
interactions.description: 25 mg of boron exceeds the UL of 20 mg/day. The multivitamin adds another 1.2 mg. Total ~26.2 mg. While boron supports testosterone and bone metabolism, excess can cause nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and at very high doses, reproductive toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Reduce to 3-10 mg/day unless directed by a physician.

interactions.title: Immune Stimulation Overload
interactions.description: This stack contains an extraordinary number of immune-stimulating compounds. Elderberry and echinacea are immune activators. Oil of oregano, garlic, and black seed oil are antimicrobials. For someone with autoimmune conditions, this level of immune stimulation could trigger or worsen flares. Echinacea is specifically cautioned in autoimmune disease.
interactions.recommendation: If there is any autoimmune history, consult an immunologist before continuing this combination.

interactions.title: Hormonal Stack Interactions
interactions.description: The Atlas X blend (horny goat weed, fenugreek, tongkat ali, nettle), plus standalone boron and saw palmetto, creates a potent hormonal combination. Fenugreek appears in both Atlas X and the Codeage multi. Saw palmetto is a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor (blocks DHT). Nettle also has anti-DHT properties. Boron raises free testosterone. These can have unpredictable hormonal effects.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor hormone levels (total/free testosterone, DHT, estradiol, SHBG). Watch for mood changes, prostate symptoms, or hair changes.

interactions.title: Iron Absorption Competition
interactions.description: The Codeage multi contains iron (27.5 mg as ferrous fumarate). Zinc (100+ mg), calcium, and magnesium all compete with iron for absorption when taken simultaneously. The very high zinc dose will significantly impair iron absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Take iron-containing supplements at a separate time from zinc, calcium, and magnesium — ideally 2+ hours apart.

interactions.title: Piperine/Black Pepper Enhances Everything
interactions.description: Black pepper (piperine) appears in the turmeric blend, beetroot blend, and cayenne in BurnSlim has similar effects. Piperine increases bioavailability of many compounds by 30-2000% by inhibiting liver and gut enzymes (CYP3A4, P-glycoprotein). This means ALL other supplements — including ibuprofen, berberine, and curcumin — may have significantly amplified effects, increasing both benefits and toxicity risks.
interactions.recommendation: Be aware that piperine potentiates the effects of virtually everything else in this stack, especially berberine and NSAIDs.

interactions.title: Oil of Oregano + Probiotics: Counterproductive
interactions.description: Oil of oregano at 6,000 mg is a potent broad-spectrum antimicrobial that kills both harmful and beneficial bacteria. Taking it with probiotics (from the probiotic blend and the Codeage multi) is counterproductive — the oregano oil will likely kill the probiotic organisms before they can colonize.
interactions.recommendation: If using oil of oregano, take probiotics at least 4-6 hours apart, or use oregano in short courses rather than continuously.

interactions.title: Redundant Olive Leaf / Moringa Sources
interactions.description: Olive leaf extract appears standalone (680 mg), as oleuropein (50 mg), and in BurnSlim (20% oleuropein olive leaf). Moringa appears standalone (1,000 mg) and in BurnSlim. This creates unnecessarily high and unpredictable total doses of both compounds, amplifying the blood-pressure-lowering and blood-sugar-lowering effects.
interactions.recommendation: Consolidate sources. Choose either standalone olive leaf or BurnSlim, not both.

interactions.title: Fenugreek Duplication & Hormonal Effects
interactions.description: Fenugreek appears in both the Atlas X blend (200 mg) and the Codeage Men's Vitality blend. Fenugreek has estrogenic compounds (diosgenin) and can affect both testosterone and estrogen levels. Double-dosing amplifies the unpredictability of hormonal effects.
interactions.recommendation: Account for total fenugreek intake from all sources.

interactions.title: Nattokinase + NSAIDs: Enhanced Fibrinolysis
interactions.description: Nattokinase is a potent fibrinolytic enzyme that breaks down fibrin (blood clots). Combined with ibuprofen's antiplatelet effects, this can dangerously impair the body's ability to stop bleeding. Bromelain (also in the tri-support) adds additional anticoagulant effects.
interactions.recommendation: Do not combine nattokinase with NSAIDs without physician guidance, especially before any surgical procedure.

interactions.title: Excessive Magnesium from Multiple Sources
interactions.description: Magnesium from L-threonate (~144 mg elemental), glycinate (~50 mg elemental from 350 mg), and the multivitamin (~15 mg) totals roughly 200+ mg of supplemental elemental magnesium. The UL for supplemental magnesium is 350 mg. While this is within limits, combined with dietary magnesium, it may cause loose stools or diarrhea.
interactions.recommendation: This level is likely fine but watch for GI symptoms. Spread doses throughout the day.

interactions.title: L-Citrulline + Beetroot: Amplified Nitric Oxide
interactions.description: L-Citrulline (200 mg in Atlas X) converts to L-arginine and then nitric oxide. Beetroot nitrates are also converted to nitric oxide. Combined with other vasodilators in the stack (magnesium, garlic, olive leaf), this could cause excessive vasodilation and blood pressure drops.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure, especially after dosing.

interactions.title: Synergistic: D3 + K2 + Magnesium + Boron
interactions.description: This is a well-designed synergistic combination. K2 directs D3-mobilized calcium to bones and away from arteries. Magnesium is required for D3 metabolism (converts D3 to active 1,25-dihydroxy form). Boron reduces urinary calcium and magnesium loss. However, the D3 dose itself is the concern — the support stack is good.
interactions.recommendation: Good combination — just address the D3 dose.

interactions.title: Synergistic: B-Vitamin Complex Coverage
interactions.description: The standalone B vitamins (B1, B2, B3, B6, B12) plus those in the multivitamin provide thorough B-complex coverage. B vitamins work synergistically and are water-soluble (excess is excreted). Benfotiamine (B1) and P5P (B6) are superior bioavailable forms. Methylcobalamin (B12) is the active form. This is a well-constructed B-vitamin protocol.
interactions.recommendation: Good selection of forms. Monitor B6 total intake — keep under 100 mg/day long-term to avoid neuropathy.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Glutathione + Vitamin C + NAC Precursors
interactions.description: Vitamin C recycles oxidized glutathione back to its active reduced form. Liposomal glutathione has better absorption than standard. This is a solid antioxidant foundation.
interactions.recommendation: Good combination for antioxidant support.
